The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3ac6296cc238bae9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 140. statement: Fix 0 < β < 1, an operator-norm bound for J∗, and fixed positive parameters in (17.2), with j(1 + η)2 < 1. On the fixed-length matrix-word events described below, every field satisfying (17.2) has a unique root y∗ of Fh. If m∗ = tanh y∗ and µh(x) ∝ exp{xT J∗x/2 + hT x}, Dh(f) = X i Eµh Var(f | x̸=i), then ∥Eµh x − m∗∥ ≤ C, ∥ Covµh (x)∥ ≤ C. (17.3) For every sufficiently small fixed ϵ > 0, every real f with N = Eµh f2 > 0, and ν = f2µh/N, |Eνx − m∗|n ≤ Cϵ + Cϵ √ n ( 1 + Dh(f) N ) . (17.4) The event and constants are independent of h and f under the stated diagnostics and stability parameters. The required word length is finite and may depend on ϵ. The same conclusions hold at j = 1 if, in addition, every approximate root in the residual region has q ≥ qmin > 0, and the inverse-word event is restricted to the diagonal class specified in Lemma 17.2. Constants may depend on qmin. This endpoint assertion is a consequence of the proof below, rather than an application of a theorem with β < 1 at β = 1.
